summary:
TimeScope is a web-based scientific investigation tool for exploring how the infrared sky changes over time using genuine NASA SPHEREx observations. Users can search by celestial coordinates, retrieve multi-epoch images, and compare spatially aligned observations through interactive playback, blinking and synchronized side-by-side visualization.

The application combines wavelength-aware observation selection, scientific metadata, alignment diagnostics and downloadable evidence reports to help users distinguish apparent temporal changes from differences in wavelength and image coverage.

Built for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, TimeScope makes astronomical time-domain exploration accessible to researchers, educators, students and citizen scientists through a reproducible, browser-based workflow.
details:
Overview

TimeScope is a web-based scientific investigation tool developed for NASA's Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. It enables users to explore genuine SPHEREx observations of the same celestial region across different acquisition times, making astronomical data more accessible to students, researchers and citizen scientists.

Key Features

  • Coordinate-based discovery and retrieval of genuine SPHEREx observations.
  • Multi-epoch image playback, blinking and synchronized side-by-side comparison.
  • Wavelength-aware observation selection and detector filtering.
  • Interactive time–wavelength graphs, scientific metadata and preliminary alignment diagnostics.
  • Downloadable scientific evidence cards and shareable investigation links.

Technical Implementation

TimeScope uses React, TypeScript and FastAPI, with Astropy, Astroquery and Reproject for scientific data processing. Genuine FITS observations are quality-masked and reprojected onto a common celestial coordinate grid, enabling consistent spatial comparisons.

The application is deployed on Google Cloud Run and incorporates bounded archive retries, historical metadata recovery and bundled observation sequences to remain useful during archive outages.

Results and Validation

TimeScope has successfully processed reference fields for all five challenge targets: Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae and R Draconis.

Data and Open Source

TimeScope uses NASA SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 observations provided by NASA/IPAC IRSA. The original application source code is released under the MIT License.

Live application: https://timescope-331427520592.us-central1.run.app/
